sentences.en: In the summer of 2003, a large crowd gathers in the state capital of South Carolina for a funeral of massive proportions.
sentences.zh: 2003年夏天，南卡罗来纳州首府聚集了大量民众，举行了一场规模宏大的葬礼。

sentences.en: There's a horse-drawn carriage that's gliding through the street with a casket in the back, draped in an American flag.
sentences.zh: 一辆马车缓缓驶过街道，车后载着一口覆盖着美国国旗的灵柩。

sentences.en: Then the casket is brought in to a large church that's ornately decorated with flowers and wreaths.
sentences.zh: 随后，灵柩被送入一座装饰着鲜花和花圈的宏大教堂。

sentences.en: We're here to honor the memory of a man whose life was rich in years,
sentences.zh: 我们在此缅怀一位人生阅历丰富的人，

sentences.en: whose career was filled with accomplishments, and whose calling was to serve his state and his country.
sentences.zh: 一位职业生涯成就斐然，且以服务州和国家为己任的人。

sentences.en: One by one, people step up to the microphone.
sentences.zh: 人们一个接一个地走上麦克风前。

sentences.en: A man who understood the art of compromise, but never at the sacrifice of principle.
sentences.zh: 他是一位深谙妥协艺术，但从不以牺牲原则为代价的人。

sentences.en: And praise the man's life and accomplishments.
sentences.zh: 大家纷纷赞颂他的人生与成就。

sentences.en: From early childhood until the day of his death, his life was governed by a strong sense of responsibility to help his fellow man.
sentences.zh: 从童年时代直到去世的那一天，他始终怀揣着强烈的责任感，致力于帮助同胞。

sentences.en: The man that they are there to eulogize is Senator Strom Thurmond, the longest-serving member in the history of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们在此悼念的人是斯特罗姆·瑟蒙德参议员，他是美国历史上任职时间最长的参议员。

sentences.en: Senate.
sentences.zh: 参议院。

sentences.en: He was a noted segregationist and open racist for much of his early career, including his opposition to the early Civil Rights Act in the 1960s
sentences.zh: 在他职业生涯的早期，他是一位著名的种族隔离主义者和公开的种族主义者，包括他在20世纪60年代反对早期的《民权法案》，

sentences.en: and his opposition to the desegregation of schools.
sentences.zh: 以及他反对学校废除种族隔离制度。

sentences.en: And so because of that history, which made Senator Thurmond a controversial figure throughout his career,
sentences.zh: 正因为这段历史，使得瑟蒙德参议员在他整个职业生涯中都是一位充满争议的人物，

sentences.en: it's a little surprising who comes to the microphone next to speak at his funeral.
sentences.zh: 所以接下来走上麦克风为他致悼词的人，着实令人有些意外。

sentences.en: Strom and I shared a life in the Senate for over 30 years.
sentences.zh: 斯特罗姆和我曾在参议院共事超过30年。

sentences.en: We shared a good life there, and it made a difference.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里共同度过了美好的时光，并有所作为。

sentences.en: It's Senator Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 那是乔·拜登参议员。

sentences.en: I disagreed deeply with Strom on the issue of civil rights and on many other issues, but I watched him change.
sentences.zh: 我在民权问题以及许多其他问题上与斯特罗姆有着深刻的分歧，但我看着他发生了改变。

sentences.en: There's a lot of moments throughout Joe Biden's longstanding political career that point to how he views the world.
sentences.zh: 在乔·拜登漫长的政治生涯中，有很多时刻体现了他看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: But this one, when he's eulogizing Strom Thurmond, I think is a unique insight to how he views himself as a bridge builder between Republicans and Democrats,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，他在为斯特罗姆·瑟蒙德致悼词的这一刻，独特地展现了他如何将自己视为共和党与民主党之间的桥梁，

sentences.en: between Black communities and white communities, and sees himself as someone who sees the best in people and can bring that out of them,
sentences.zh: 以及黑人社区与白人社区之间的桥梁，他认为自己是一个能发现他人优点并将其激发出来的人，

sentences.en: even as his own party and maybe sometimes his own supporters doubt it.
sentences.zh: 即便是在他所在的党派，甚至有时是他自己的支持者对此表示怀疑的时候。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Part four in our series on pivotal moments in the lives of the top four Democratic candidates for president.
sentences.zh: 这是我们关于四位民主党总统候选人人生关键时刻系列报道的第四部分。

sentences.en: Today, Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 今天的主角是乔·拜登。

sentences.en: It's Friday, December 20th.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月20日，星期五。

sentences.en: Estet Herndon, you pointed us to this moment, when Biden is at Strom Thurmond's funeral, eulogizing him, as particularly revealing of who he is as a candidate today.
sentences.zh: 埃斯特·赫恩登，你向我们指出了这个时刻，即拜登在斯特罗姆·瑟蒙德的葬礼上为他致悼词，这特别能揭示他作为当今候选人的特质。

sentences.en: And we repeatedly invited Joe Biden to tell us his story himself.
sentences.zh: 我们曾多次邀请乔·拜登亲自向我们讲述他的故事。

sentences.en: But of the four Democratic presidential candidates that we decided to profile, he's the only one to have declined to participate.
sentences.zh: 但在我们决定报道的四位民主党总统候选人中，他是唯一拒绝参与的一位。

sentences.en: So where do you think that this story starts for Joe Biden?
sentences.zh: 那么，你认为乔·拜登的故事是从哪里开始的呢？

sentences.en: Well, for Biden, I think the story starts in the 1960s in Wilmington, Delaware.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对于拜登来说，我认为故事始于20世纪60年代的特拉华州威尔明顿。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: The Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King, 39 years old and a Nobel Peace Prize winner, and the leader of the nonviolent civil rights movement in the United States,
sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金博士，39岁，诺贝尔和平奖得主，美国非暴力民权运动的领袖，

sentences.en: was assassinated in Memphis tonight.
sentences.zh: 今晚在孟菲斯遇刺身亡。

sentences.en: After the assassination of Martin Luther King...
sentences.zh: 在马丁·路德·金遇刺后……

sentences.en: The National Guard was called out in several cities to put down riots.
sentences.zh: 国民警卫队被派往多个城市以平息骚乱。

sentences.en: One of these cities was Wilmington, Delaware.
sentences.zh: 其中一个城市就是特拉华州的威尔明顿。

sentences.en: Wilmington was one of the cities that experienced riots, that changed the landscape of the city forever.
sentences.zh: 威尔明顿是经历过骚乱的城市之一，那场骚乱永远改变了这座城市的面貌。

sentences.en: And those riots really built on the racial tension that was already existing in Delaware.
sentences.zh: 那些骚乱实际上加剧了特拉华州本已存在的种族紧张局势。

sentences.en: But now, in Wilmington, the National Guard is still on duty, and the governor, Charles Terry, has no plan to send it back.
sentences.zh: 但现在，在威尔明顿，国民警卫队仍在执勤，而州长查尔斯·特里并没有撤军的计划。

sentences.en: Now, folks may not know this, but Delaware has always had a pretty racially fraught history.
sentences.zh: 人们可能不知道，特拉华州一直有着相当严重的种族历史问题。

sentences.en: The southern portions, particularly, have been compared to the more Confederate South.
sentences.zh: 尤其是南部地区，常被拿来与南方邦联地区相提并论。

sentences.en: It would not be surprising, according to folks at the time, to see Confederate flags there.
sentences.zh: 据当时的人们说，在那里看到邦联旗帜并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: And it was one of the cities and regions that were deeply involved in the desegregation fights that culminated with Brown versus Board of Education.
sentences.zh: 它是深度参与废除种族隔离斗争的城市和地区之一，这场斗争最终以“布朗诉教育委员会案”告终。

sentences.en: And in those northern portions of Delaware, in the suburbs of Wilmington, you have the more liberal areas, and the places that fuel the Democratic electorates.
sentences.zh: 而在特拉华州的北部，在威尔明顿的郊区，则是较为自由的地区，也是民主党选民的聚集地。

sentences.en: So Wilmington is caught in between those two worlds.
sentences.zh: 所以威尔明顿夹在这两个世界之间。

sentences.en: — It's in that tension, it's in the context of that tension, that Joe Biden gets involved in politics.
sentences.zh: ——正是在这种紧张局势中，在那种紧张局势的背景下，乔·拜登投身于政治。

sentences.en: — And who is Joe Biden in this moment?
sentences.zh: ——那么当时的乔·拜登是怎样一个人？

sentences.en: — He was a lot of things.
sentences.zh: ——他有很多面。

sentences.en: He was a son of Delaware, and also someone who had legitimate relationships in Black communities in Wilmington.
sentences.zh: 他是特拉华州的儿子，也是在威尔明顿黑人社区中拥有真实人脉的人。

sentences.en: That included longstanding friendships from his time as a lifeguard at the Black swimming pool in town.
sentences.zh: 这包括他担任镇上黑人游泳池救生员时结下的长期友谊。

sentences.en: But it also included relationships with civil rights activists, including the leaders who led some of the civil rights protests and marches for school desegregation.
sentences.zh: 但也包括与民权活动人士的关系，其中包括领导了一些争取学校废除种族隔离的民权抗议和游行的领袖。

sentences.en: — Mm-hmm.
— So when the city is going through this tumultuous period,
sentences.zh: ——所以当城市经历这段动荡时期时，

sentences.en: Biden sees those relationships as something that makes him unique in the community, and something that positions him to make change.
sentences.zh: 拜登将这些关系视为使他在社区中独一无二的特质，也是他能够做出改变的资本。

sentences.en: So he decides to get involved in politics.
sentences.zh: 于是他决定投身政治。

sentences.en: He moves from law to run for the city council, and then later for the Senate in 1971.
sentences.zh: 他从法律界转行竞选市议员，随后在1971年竞选参议员。

sentences.en: — I'm Joe Biden, and I'm a candidate for the United States Senate.
sentences.zh: ——我是乔·拜登，我是美国参议院的候选人。

sentences.en: — And then that Senate race, he leans on those relationships to craft a new brand of politician in the state.
sentences.zh: ——在那场参议院竞选中，他利用这些关系在该州打造了一种全新的政治人物形象。

sentences.en: — Do you believe politicians when they tell you something in an election year?
sentences.zh: ——在选举年，当政客们对你做出承诺时，你相信他们吗？

sentences.en: — No.
sentences.zh: ——不信。

sentences.en: — Most of the time, no.
sentences.zh: ——大多数时候，不信。

sentences.en: — No comment.
sentences.zh: ——无可奉告。

sentences.en: — That's what we've come to.
sentences.zh: ——这就是我们现在的处境。

sentences.en: — It's a type of politician that is emblematic of generational change and can tell Wilmington,
sentences.zh: ——这是一种象征着代际变革的政治人物，他可以告诉威尔明顿人：

sentences.en: I'm not like those white politicians of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我与过去那些白人政客不同。

sentences.en: — Politicians have done such a job on the people that the people don't believe them anymore.
sentences.zh: ——政客们把民众伤得太深，以至于民众不再相信他们了。

sentences.en: And I'd like a shot at changing that.
sentences.zh: 我想尝试改变这一点。

sentences.en: — I come from your community, I know your community, and I'll legislate in your intereSt.
sentences.zh: ——我来自你们的社区，我了解你们的社区，我将为你们的利益立法。

sentences.en: That's his pitch to voters, that in this time when there is legitimate tension between Wilmington and the rest of the state, between kind of Black communities
sentences.zh: 这就是他向选民兜售的理念：在这个威尔明顿与该州其他地区、黑人社区与白人社区之间存在真实紧张关系的时代，

sentences.en: and white communities, he's someone who has good relationships in both.
sentences.zh: 他是一个在两边都有良好关系的人。

sentences.en: And that pitch to Delaware voters worked.
sentences.zh: 而这一向特拉华州选民兜售的理念奏效了。

sentences.en: Joe Biden was elected by a tiny margin,
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登以微弱优势当选，

sentences.en: 50 to 49, and he came to the Senate to embody that new type of politician that he sold himself as.
sentences.zh: 50比49，他进入参议院，体现了他所标榜的那种新型政治人物。

sentences.en: And as a new senator, he's trying to figure out how to navigate a Washington that really runs on personal relationships at this time.
sentences.zh: 作为一名新任参议员，他试图弄清楚如何驾驭当时完全依赖个人关系的华盛顿。

sentences.en: Joe Biden, fresh and new, is trying to figure out what he can accomplish and also how he can serve those dual constituencies, the Black and white communities in Delaware.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登，作为新人，正试图弄清楚他能完成什么，以及如何服务于特拉华州的黑人和白人这两个双重选民群体。

sentences.en: And one of the issues he decides to focus on is crime.
sentences.zh: 他决定关注的议题之一是犯罪。

sentences.en: — And why crime?
sentences.zh: ——为什么是犯罪？

sentences.en: Why that issue?
sentences.zh: 为什么是那个议题？

sentences.en: — So, since those riots in the 60s, there has been a fear around crime in Wilmington.
sentences.zh: ——所以，自60年代的骚乱以来，威尔明顿一直笼罩在对犯罪的恐惧之中。

sentences.en: Some founded, some unfounded.
sentences.zh: 有些是有根据的，有些则不然。

sentences.en: But as you move throughout the decade, particularly through the 70s, there is a kind of more increasing nationwide focus on the presence of drugs.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，特别是进入70年代，全国范围内对毒品问题的关注日益增加。

sentences.en: — America's public enemy number one in the United States is drug abuse.
sentences.zh: ——美国的第一公敌是毒品滥用。

sentences.en: In order to fight and defeat this enemy, it is necessary to wage a new all-out offensive.
sentences.zh: 为了打击并战胜这个敌人，必须发动一场新的全面攻势。

sentences.en: — And an increasing violent crime rate.
sentences.zh: ——以及不断上升的暴力犯罪率。

sentences.en: That is kind of a whisper in the 70s that grows to a full-blown chorus by the 80s.
sentences.zh: 这在70年代还只是一种低语，到了80年代就演变成了全社会的呼声。

sentences.en: — It is a war.
sentences.zh: ——这是一场战争。

sentences.en: Cops against gangs.
sentences.zh: 警察对抗帮派。

sentences.en: Gangs against cops.
sentences.zh: 帮派对抗警察。

sentences.en: — Compared to this time last year, the overall crime rate is up by 11 percent.
sentences.zh: ——与去年同期相比，总体犯罪率上升了11%。

sentences.en: — Nearly 3,000 people killed and 15,000 wounded since 1980.
— Auto theft up by almost 18 percent.
sentences.zh: ——汽车盗窃案上升了近18%。

sentences.en: — Whole neighborhoods of Los Angeles live in fear.
sentences.zh: ——洛杉矶的整个社区都生活在恐惧之中。

sentences.en: — Many police departments say they're caught in the middle between budget cutbacks, manpower shortages, and what appears to be a national crime epidemic.
sentences.zh: ——许多警察局表示，他们夹在预算削减、人手短缺和看似全国性的犯罪流行病之间，左右为难。

sentences.en: — There was a national panic around drugs and drug dealing.
sentences.zh: ——当时全国范围内对毒品和毒品交易感到恐慌。

sentences.en: There was a national panic around violent crime.
sentences.zh: 全国范围内对暴力犯罪感到恐慌。

sentences.en: And this crosses racial lines.
sentences.zh: 这跨越了种族界限。

sentences.en: — It is by far the most critical problem in the cities of America, large and small.
sentences.zh: ——这无疑是美国大大小小城市中最关键的问题。

sentences.en: — Both white and black leaders were seeing their communities upended.
sentences.zh: ——白人和黑人领袖都目睹了他们的社区被颠覆。

sentences.en: — I'm not talking about heart disease, sickle cell anemia, high blood pressure.
sentences.zh: ——我说的不是心脏病、镰状细胞性贫血、高血压。

sentences.en: I'm a physician, but I'm talking about homicides, the leading cause of death for young black men.
sentences.zh: 我是一名医生，但我说的是凶杀案，这是导致年轻黑人男性死亡的首要原因。

sentences.en: — Seeing their communities really ravaged.
sentences.zh: ——目睹他们的社区被彻底蹂躏。

sentences.en: — They're killing our people.
sentences.zh: ——他们在杀害我们的人民。

sentences.en: They're destroying our neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 他们在摧毁我们的社区。

sentences.en: They're eroding our social fabric.
sentences.zh: 他们在侵蚀我们的社会结构。

sentences.en: They're crippling our cities.
sentences.zh: 他们在瘫痪我们的城市。

sentences.en: — And we're looking for the federal government to intervene and do something about it.
sentences.zh: ——我们期待联邦政府介入并采取行动。

sentences.en: So with this issue that cuts across race,
sentences.zh: 所以，面对这个跨越种族的问题，

sentences.en: Biden sees a political opportunity for himself and for the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 拜登为自己和民主党看到了政治机遇。

sentences.en: For himself, he sees a chance to really hone in on an issue that can appease both black and white communities and insulate himself for what was going to be a tough re-election
sentences.zh: 对他个人而言，他看到了一个机会，可以专注于一个既能安抚黑人社区又能安抚白人社区的议题，并为他即将到来的艰难连任竞选提供保障，

sentences.en: in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 在参议院中。

sentences.en: And for the Democratic Party, he thinks he can change the reputation that Democrats have as being soft on crime.
sentences.zh: 而对于民主党，他认为可以改变民主党在犯罪问题上软弱的声誉。

sentences.en: He sees focusing on this issue as an opportunity to broaden the Democrats' national appeal and actually become the leaders on reforming the criminal justice system.
sentences.zh: 他将关注这一议题视为扩大民主党全国影响力的机会，并真正成为刑事司法系统改革的领导者。

sentences.en: — So what does he actually do now that he's landed on this issue as his focus?
sentences.zh: ——那么，既然他已经将此作为重点，他实际上做了什么？

sentences.en: — So Biden works his way on to the most important committee that focuses on this issue, the Senate Judiciary Committee.
sentences.zh: ——拜登设法进入了关注此议题的最重要委员会——参议院司法委员会。

sentences.en: And for him to accomplish anything, he knows that he needs to have working relationships with Republicans who at this point are in the majority and control the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他知道，要取得任何成就，就必须与当时占多数并控制参议院的共和党人建立工作关系。

sentences.en: And the number one person who could impact
sentences.zh: 而那个能影响

sentences.en: Biden's ability to pass legislation on the Senate Judiciary Committee is its chairman.
sentences.zh: 拜登在参议院司法委员会通过立法能力的第一人，就是委员会主席。

sentences.en: — The committee will come to order.
sentences.zh: ——委员会现在开会。

sentences.en: — Senator Strom Thurmond of South Carolina.
sentences.zh: ——南卡罗来纳州的斯特罗姆·瑟蒙德参议员。

sentences.en: — Unfortunately, the state of our criminal justice today favors the criminal.
sentences.zh: ——不幸的是，我们今天的刑事司法状况偏袒了罪犯。

sentences.en: — Strom Thurmond, like many conservative
sentences.zh: ——斯特罗姆·瑟蒙德，像当时许多保守派

sentences.en: Republicans at the time, has that law and order streak.
sentences.zh: 共和党人一样，有着那种维护法律与秩序的倾向。

sentences.en: — Our public safety officers are standing as a thin blue line, sheltering us from criminal anarchy.
sentences.zh: ——我们的公共安全官员正作为一道薄薄的蓝色防线，保护我们免受犯罪无政府状态的侵害。

sentences.en: — And has always thought that the way to kind of combat lawlessness was through the expansion of the prison system.
sentences.zh: ——并且一直认为打击无法无天的方式是通过扩大监狱系统。

sentences.en: — Today, the criminal has four chances in five never to be arrested.
sentences.zh: ——今天，罪犯有五分之四的机会永远不会被逮捕。

sentences.en: A person arrested has five chances out of six not to save time in prison.
sentences.zh: 被捕的人有六分之五的机会不用在监狱里服刑。

sentences.en: Only about one criminal in 30 ends up behind bars.
sentences.zh: 只有大约30个罪犯中才有1个最终入狱。

sentences.en: — But let's remember,
